title: Example observable types and scoped meanings

items.title: Example observable types and scoped meanings
items.statement:
Use the framework-local unit and domain dictionary of
[[def-qft-framework-units]] and the energy, SI/natural-unit, and finite-matrix
conventions of [[def-qft-example-data]]. A physical quantity is always typed
relative to the selected QFT formulation and its declared model data; its name
or units alone do not identify it with a quantity in another formulation.

For the **exact finite-regulator class** used on this page, the state space is
the finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$ for an integer
$d\ge1$. Model inputs include the selected Hermitian Hamiltonian matrices,
their time-dependent Hermitian interaction when present, a dimensionless
coupling parameter, an initial state, and an explicitly supplied finite
outcome measurement. A pure initial state is a vector $\psi\in\mathbb C^d$
with $\|\psi\|=1$; a mixed state is a matrix $\rho=\rho^*$ with
$\langle\rho v,v\rangle\ge0$ for every $v$ and $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$.
An exact regulated observable on this finite space is a specified Hermitian
matrix $O=O^*$ with a declared physical unit. The matrix and state are model
data; the measurement procedure and any physical rule assigning outcomes are
additional data. This definition does not say that an operator symbol by
itself is a detector outcome or probability.

A **finite probability law** on the declared outcome set
$\{1,\ldots,m\}$, $m\ge1$, is a vector $(p_1,\ldots,p_m)$ with
$p_a\ge0$ and $\sum_{a=1}^m p_a=1$. It is a mathematical type. Assigning that
law to a particular preparation and measurement is a separate physical
postulate. A prediction derived from an actually constructed regulated model
is conditional on those inputs and the adopted rule.

A **formal coefficient record** is a sequence $(c_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of
specified coefficients, sometimes displayed as the symbol
$\sum_{n\ge0}c_n\lambda^n$. Unless convergence and an evaluation map are
separately proved and adopted, the symbol records coefficients only: it is not
an evaluated function, exact probability, convergent perturbation series, or
error bound. A formal coefficient can be assigned a phenomenological meaning
only by a separate, model-specific physical adoption with its approximation
scope stated.

An **empirical estimate** is a source-reported number obtained by analyzing a
finite record of measurement outcomes under the stated preparation, apparatus,
calibration, sampling, and analysis conditions. Its reported uncertainty and
conditions travel with the estimate. It is not the exact model value, and it
does not prove the framework used to interpret it. The 2022 Fan et al. report
is an example of a source-reported electron magnetic-moment determination;
this definition supplies no numerical result, uncertainty reconstruction, or
new experimental claim.

Primitive and derived status is formulation-relative. In a selected regulated
model, the regulator, Hamiltonian data, coupling, initial state, and supplied
measurement are declared inputs; an evolution, amplitude, or probability law
is derived only when the construction and adopted rule establish it. In a
formal calculation, the specified masses, couplings, coefficient rules, and
subtraction prescription are inputs, while its listed coefficients are
derived within that formal calculation. An empirical estimate is a reported
data-analysis result, not a primitive model parameter or a theorem.

The following units are examples of types, not identifications of quantities:
a cross section $\sigma$ is area-valued with SI unit $\mathrm{m^2}$; a rate
$\Gamma$ is inverse-time-valued with unit $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; an energy width
$\Gamma_E$ has unit joule. Only a separately stated convention may identify
$\Gamma_E=\hbar\Gamma$. The fine-structure parameter $\alpha$, a dimensionless
coupling $g$, and a gyromagnetic factor $g_s$ are dimensionless but have
different physical meanings. The name “width,” a common symbol, or matching
dimensions does not supply an exponential-decay law or an equality between
these parameters.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, §0.1 “Units and Scales”
X. Fan et al., Measurement of the Electron Magnetic Moment, Physical Review Letters 130, 071801 (2023), arXiv:2209.13084v2 (2022)

items.physical_scope: Framework-local primitive/derived, unit, observable, formal-coefficient, and empirical-data distinctions for the finite regulated examples and specified formal calculations on this page. No general continuum observable, detector, scattering, or empirical-estimator construction is asserted.

items.title: Exact regulated transition probabilities and controlled coefficients
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), and use the finite regulated model type of
[[def-qft-example-observable-types]]. Let $d\ge1$, let $\tau>0$ be a time
interval endpoint in seconds, let $\hbar>0$ have unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and
let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless. Let
$H_0=H_0^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have unit joule and let
$V:[0,\tau]\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ be norm-continuous, Hermitian-valued, and
joule-valued. Set
$$V_I(t)=e^{itH_0/\hbar}V(t)e^{-itH_0/\hbar},\qquad B=\sup_{0\le t\le\tau}\|V_I(t)\|,\qquad z=\frac{|\lambda|B\tau}{\hbar}.$$
Define $S_0(t)=I$ and
$$S_{n+1}(t)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_0^tV_I(r)S_n(r)\,dr,\qquad S(t)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\lambda^nS_n(t).$$
For $W\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, **unitary** means $W^*W=WW^*=I$.
Write $U(\tau)=e^{-iH_0\tau/\hbar}S(\tau)$ and, for $N\ge0$,
$$U_N(\tau)=e^{-iH_0\tau/\hbar}\sum_{n=0}^N\lambda^nS_n(\tau),\qquad R_N=e^z\frac{z^{N+1}}{(N+1)!}.$$

Let $\psi\in\mathbb C^d$ be a unit initial vector. A supplied finite
projective measurement is a family $P_1,\ldots,P_m\in M_d(\mathbb C)$,
$m\ge1$, satisfying $P_a=P_a^*=P_a^2$, $P_aP_b=0$ for $a\ne b$, and
$\sum_{a=1}^mP_a=I$. Equivalently, the one-Kraus-per-outcome data
$M_{a,1}=P_a$ form a normalized finite instrument in the sense of
[[def-qft-finite-bounded-kraus-instrument]]. Adopt the constructed-model Born
interpretation of [[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]] only for this
actually constructed finite model and measurement. For its physical reading,
also adopt the explicit preparation/evolution assumption [A3]: the initial
density is $\rho_0:=T_{\psi,\psi}$, and the model density at the measurement
time is $\rho_\tau:=U(\tau)\rho_0U(\tau)^*=T_{U(\tau)\psi,U(\tau)\psi}$.
Here $T_{u,v}$ is the rank-one map $x\mapsto\langle x,v\rangle u$ of
[[lem-qft-finite-instrument-normalization]]. The Dyson result proves that this
matrix $U(\tau)$ is unitary; identifying it with the selected model's state
update is an adopted physical assumption, not a conclusion about nature.
Define the exact model probability and the truncated squared norm by
$$p_a=\|P_aU(\tau)\psi\|^2,\qquad q_{a,N}=\|P_aU_N(\tau)\psi\|^2.$$
Then $p_a\in[0,1]$, $\sum_ap_a=1$, and
$$|p_a-q_{a,N}|\le\bigl(2\sqrt{q_{a,N}}+R_N\bigr)R_N.$$
The nonnegative number $q_{a,N}$ is a truncation-derived square, not generally
a probability.

For the exact finite interaction matrix write $S(\tau;\lambda)=I+i\mathsf T(\lambda)$
and $\mathsf T(\lambda)=\lambda\mathsf T_1+\lambda^2\mathsf T_2+\cdots$.
Use the standard basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ for matrix entries, so
$\mathsf T_{fi}:=e_f^*\mathsf T e_i$ for $1\le f,i\le d$. For a matrix
$A$, define its Hermitian imaginary part by
$\operatorname{Im}_{\mathrm H}A:=(A-A^*)/(2i)$. Exact unitarity gives
$$2\operatorname{Im}\mathsf T_{ii}(\lambda)=\sum_{f=1}^d|\mathsf T_{fi}(\lambda)|^2,\qquad \mathsf T_1=\mathsf T_1^*,\qquad 2\operatorname{Im}_{\mathrm H}\mathsf T_2=\mathsf T_1^*\mathsf T_1.$$
These are finite-regulator coefficient identities, not continuum optical or
scattering theorems.

In the two-level case $H_0=0$, $\lambda=1$, and
$V(t)=g_E\sigma_x$ with $g_E>0$ in joules and
$\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, the exact transition
probability from $e_1=(1,0)$ to the projector $P=|e_2\rangle\langle e_2|$
is $\sin^2z$, where the previously defined $z$ equals $g_E\tau/\hbar$
because $V_I=V$ and $\|\sigma_x\|=1$; the first-order squared transition
coefficient is $z^2$ and may exceed $1$. For all real $z$,
$$|\sin^2z-z^2|\le\frac{|z|^4}{3}.$$
The exact survival factor is $\cos^2z$, which is not $e^{-\Gamma\tau}$ for
any $\Gamma>0$ on all $\tau\ge0$.

For the occupation truncation with orthonormal basis
$e_0,\ldots,e_N$, define $a_Ne_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}$ (zero for $n=0$),
$a_N^*e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1}$ for $n<N$, and $a_N^*e_N=0$. Then
$$[a_N,a_N^*]=I-(N+1)|e_N\rangle\langle e_N|.$$
More generally, no finite-dimensional matrices $A,B$ satisfy $[A,B]=I$.
These exact regulator facts assert neither an infinite-dimensional CCR
construction nor a continuum limit.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 3 “Interacting Fields,” §3.1.1 “Dyson’s Formula”
J. Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, author-hosted prepublication manuscript, §§2.3.1–2.3.2
R. B. Griffiths, Notes on Quantum Information Theory, complete §7

items.physical_scope: Exact deductions in an explicitly constructed finite-dimensional regulated model with a supplied finite projective measurement, an adopted pure-state update by the constructed unitary, and the constructed-model Born postulate. Finite-order squares are not generally probabilities. No continuum QFT, regulator removal, asymptotic scattering operator, empirical result, or sample-based inference is asserted.

items.title: Exact two-level transition versus its first coefficient
items.statement:
Under the explicit pure-state preparation and unitary-evolution assumption of
[[pthm-qft-example-regulated-probability-control]], take
$\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$, $H_0=0$, $V(t)=g_E\sigma_x$ with
$g_E>0$ joules, dimensionless $\lambda=1$, initial vector $e_1=(1,0)$, and
the two-outcome projective measurement $P=|e_2\rangle\langle e_2|$,
$I-P$, where $e_2=(0,1)$. At
$\tau=\pi\hbar/(2g_E)$ seconds the exact model transition probability is
$1$, whereas the first-order squared transition coefficient is
$\pi^2/4>1$. The latter is a coefficient-derived square, not a probability.
This is an exact constructed-model calculation, not a simulated or reported
experiment.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 3 “Interacting Fields,” §3.1.1 “Dyson’s Formula”

items.physical_scope: One exactly constructed two-level finite Hamiltonian and its explicitly supplied projective measurement. The first-order squared coefficient is not called a probability, and no continuum decay or experimental data is claimed.

items.title: One-mode time-ordered correlator versus retarded response
items.statement:
For the exact single oscillator mode of
[[lem-qft-example-oscillator-feynman-prescription]], let $\omega>0$ in
$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ and choose $t=-\pi/(2\omega)$. The normalized
time-ordered vacuum correlator is $-i/(2\omega)$, while the retarded response
kernel is $0$. The correlator at negative time is not a response to a future
source. This fixed-mode calculation does not establish a spatial-causality or
superluminal-signalling result.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, §§2.1.1 and 2.7.1–2.7.2
M. Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted prepublication draft, §7 oscillator two-point kernel and frequency prescription

items.physical_scope: One exact oscillator mode with the stated core, vacuum, and conventions. The negative-time correlation differs from a retarded response; this makes no spatial-locality, signalling, interacting-field, or empirical claim.
